reason: Thread and planks may make a binding or support for gathering the studies.
expectation: I expect some kind of bookbinding component, though its exact purpose is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Paper at the library table could help assemble the records, but I want to make the binding first.

effect: Thread and planks made a loom, so my binding guess was wrong. I'll try preparing the paper at the library table.
reaction: The loom surprised me; its role in gathering studies is unclear.
reason: Paper seems useful for assembling the studies at the library table.
expectation: I expect the paper to be placed at the table for a later combination.

effect: The paper is at the library table, enabling a combination with planks.
reaction: The next step is clear, though I don't yet know what the planks will make.
reason: Combining the planks with the paper is the only offered constructive action and may help gather the studies.
expectation: I expect an assembly or support for the papers, though its exact form is uncertain.

effect: The paper-lined boards provide four named slots for the studies, so I can begin gathering them.
reaction: The protective boards make their purpose clear.
reason: The botanical sheets fit the Plants slot and advance the gathering goal.
expectation: I expect the botanical sheets to fill the Plants slot in the binding boards.

effect: The botanical sheets are fitted into the boards, leaving three studies to gather.
reason: The pond drawings are another required study and fit the remaining Pond life slot.
expectation: I expect the pond drawings to be fitted into the binding boards.

effect: The pond drawings are fitted, leaving the weather record and star chart to gather.
reason: The weather record fills one of the remaining study slots.
expectation: I expect the weather record to be fitted into the binding boards.

effect: The weather record is fitted, leaving the star chart as the final study.
reaction: The repeated fittings are straightforward, though becoming a little repetitive.
reason: The star chart fills the last named slot and is the only offered constructive action.
expectation: I expect the star chart to be fitted into the binding boards, completing the gathering goal.

effect: The star chart completed the collection, revealing the goal to bind the encyclopedia.
reaction: The new binding step gives the gathered studies a clear purpose.
reason: Thread can sew the collected sheets into the boards, and this is the only offered constructive action.
expectation: I expect the thread to bind the studies into an encyclopedia.

effect: Thread bound the four studies into an encyclopedia, completing the chapter.
reaction: The finished volume gives the earlier observations a useful home.

mostWorthwhile.text: Binding the encyclopedia brought the separate studies together for consultation, giving the collection a clear purpose.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the studies one at a time became repetitive, even though the slots made each action clear.

surprise.text: Thread and planks made a loom rather than the binding component I expected; its role in this chapter remained unclear.

arbitrary.text: Making the loom felt disconnected from the stated goal, since its purpose was not explained or used in the completed sequence.

continue.text: I might continue if another chapter offered more consequential choices; assembling the encyclopedia was satisfying, but the repeated fittings offered little to decide.
